author: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
locator: Release date August 12, 2026; Table 2 (chokepoint volumes) and Table 4 (Strait of Hormuz oil and LNG, 1Q25–2Q26); methodology note on AIS reliability
notes: EIA estimates show total oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz falling from 21.6 mb/d in 4Q25 to 14.9 mb/d in 1Q26 and 4.9 mb/d in 2Q26, and LNG flows from 10.5 Bcf/d in 4Q25 to 7.4 Bcf/d in 1Q26 and 0.8 Bcf/d in 2Q26, after military action began Feb 28, 2026. EIA states AIS signal data for Hormuz became 'especially unreliable' from late February 2026 and that 2026 Hormuz volumes are revised frequently — so the 4.9 mb/d figure is an estimate of a severe constriction, not a metered zero-flow blockade.

title: Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026 — Global Energy Security Data (Strait of Hormuz tables)
